note: Personal stories from public submissions. Placed at locality level, never at an address. Reviewed by SB.

stories.site: Western Downs Digital Park — Dalby (Zerra DC)
stories.name: Celia Karp
stories.quote: Our family have been operating the same farm since the late 1940’s. The idea of siting a Data Centre/Digital Park (quoted as being the largest in Australia) in a depleted groundwater area; a region noted for its propensity for regular droughts, is beyond comprehension. The optics of a State/Local Government supporting a Data Digital Park in this region shows our politicians in the worst possible light; totally contemptuous of local farmers who've been striving for more than a generation under difficult climatic conditions, drought and flood, fighting for their livelihoods to provide future food security and export income.
stories.source: Submission to Western Downs Regional Council, published on the council's Development.i portal

stories.site: Western Downs Digital Park — Dalby (Zerra DC)
stories.name: Emma O'Connor
stories.quote: I am the daughter of Thomas and Michelle O’Connor, who own and farm [the farm]. It is a cattle and grain farm and has been in my family since 1965. I am one of four children.

stories.site: Western Downs Digital Park — Dalby (Zerra DC)
stories.name: Joel Holtham
stories.quote: This is where I always return to, it's where my family and support network reside, and it's where my mother was buried. The fact that this AI Data Centre is being considered for the Western Downs is abhorrent and extremely worrying for the future of the region. Key information is missing.
stories.source: Submission to Western Downs Regional Council, published on the council's Development.i portal

stories.site: Western Downs Digital Park — Dalby (Zerra DC)
stories.name: Norma Farrant
stories.quote: Our home is about 4km from the proposed site in a straight line and 14km by road. We rely on bore water for household use. On some days we can already hear vehicle activity and smell the existing Wambo Feedlot from our home.
stories.source: Submission to Western Downs Regional Council, published on the council's Development.i portal

stories.site: Western Downs Digital Park — Dalby (Zerra DC)
stories.name: Name not given
stories.quote: I’m a born and bred Dalby Girl who has also lived in many other Towns and States across Australia – returning to Dalby 4 years ago with my family. Although Industry has grown significantly in the region in the last 40 years and allowed the spread of risk over many areas instead of the former sole concentration on the Grain Industry we seem to only be currently looking at the dollars and forgetting about safety, risk, environment etc and completely dismissing the voice of the Residents who are then saddled with the effects of decisions for generations to come. My position - I object to this application and ask Council to request the Applicant to provide the missing information listed below …
stories.source: Submission to Western Downs Regional Council, published on the council's Development.i portal

stories.site: Western Downs Digital Park — Dalby (Zerra DC)
stories.name: Janine Brownie
stories.quote: My husband has rheumatoid arthritis and over the last years has been unable to continue working. We moved to Tara initially as it was one of the few regions where we could buy property and be mortgage free. I am still working remotely from the property.
stories.source: Submission to Western Downs Regional Council, published on the council's Development.i portal

stories.site: Western Downs Digital Park — Dalby (Zerra DC)
stories.name: Lynda von Pein
stories.quote: Our family has been in involved in agriculture in the Kogan area for 53 years and we foresee the next generation continuing agriculture on our property in the future. We already have gas pipelines and gas wells on our property as well as a gas processing plant neighbouring our property. There have been so many issues that we have come across over the years with the gas and we find it hard to trust these huge companies.
stories.source: Submission to Western Downs Regional Council, published on the council's Development.i portal

stories.site: Western Downs Digital Park — Dalby (Zerra DC)
stories.name: Joshua Pukallus
stories.quote: I have lived in Dalby for five years since finishing my education here, and my family has lived in this area for four generations. I have always loved the community and support this region can offer, and what I can give back to. As such, I’m not impressed by a foreign tech company deciding this region is a suitable place to extract from.
stories.source: Submission to Western Downs Regional Council, published on the council's Development.i portal

stories.site: Western Downs Digital Park — Dalby (Zerra DC)
stories.name: Julie Wallin
stories.quote: I live on the other side of town. As a resident, I believe I will be impacted by water, electricity, and infrastructure changes and price increase and disruptions, as this AI plant will add extra environmental problems to what is already a busy area. Also there is no guarantee the 1500 jobs will be given to local people.
stories.source: Submission to Western Downs Regional Council, published on the council's Development.i portal

stories.site: Western Downs Digital Park — Dalby (Zerra DC)
stories.name: Ali Briggs
stories.quote: I grew up on next door to that property, on the Braemar Creek. I know the dirt isn't the best and that it's really dry. But still people, animals and plants call it home.
stories.source: Submission to Western Downs Regional Council, published on the council's Development.i portal

stories.site: Western Downs Digital Park — Dalby (Zerra DC)
stories.name: Jane Yorkston
stories.quote: I grew up on the Darling Downs and have family living in Dalby. I am incredibly concerned about the water usage of this proposed development in an agricultural area and also about possible effects on the Condamine Darling River system. We need a life supporting environment more than we need a data centre & A1.
stories.source: Submission to Western Downs Regional Council, published on the council's Development.i portal

stories.site: Western Downs Digital Park — Dalby (Zerra DC)
stories.name: Tina Williams
stories.quote: I’m not positive how all of this will exactly affect me, my children, and my grandchildren, who all reside in Dalby. I know, what I’ve read, and heard. It’s not good, in fact, it scares the hell out of me.
stories.source: Submission to Western Downs Regional Council, published on the council's Development.i portal

stories.site: Western Downs Digital Park — Dalby (Zerra DC)
stories.name: Liezel Maloney
stories.quote: The Western Downs is our home, and decisions of this magnitude will affect residents and future generations for decades. I therefore formally object to the proposed development and request that my submission be considered in full before Council makes its decision. Please acknowledge receipt of this email and confirm that it has been registered as a formal submission against Development Application DA 030.2026.513.001.
stories.source: Submission to Western Downs Regional Council, published on the council's Development.i portal

stories.site: Western Downs Digital Park — Dalby (Zerra DC)
stories.name: Denver Kanowski
stories.quote: I'm sure you are aware that if that status is granted then the local government, & residents, would be locked out of any input on the future of our land which will be affected by this project -fait accompli for the multi nationals. I view this proposal with grave concern & request serious consideration by Council including our elected councillors. Please forward this email & any information available to them for consideration.
stories.source: Submission to Western Downs Regional Council, published on the council's Development.i portal
